passage: Note from Yash, for Rashmi's mother while she rests. Dadi arrived this afternoon with a bag of sweets and a rattle. She walked past the crib, crouched down and hugged Rashmi first. "You are my special one," she said. Rashmi's face lit up and she leaned right into her shoulder. Only then did Dadi go and look at the baby. Later Rashmi carried the rattle to the crib herself and showed it to her. I think this helped her feel safe.

qa.q: What did Dadi bring with her?
qa.a: She brought a bag of sweets and a rattle.

qa.q: How was Rashmi feeling when she leaned into Dadi's shoulder?
qa.a: She felt safe and important again. Her face lighting up shows that being hugged first meant a lot.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that protects an older child during a new-baby time?
qa.a: She noticed Rashmi first, hugged her and told her she is special before looking at the baby, so Rashmi did not feel replaced.

qa.q: How might Rashmi's mother feel when she reads Yash's note?
qa.a: She is probably relieved and grateful, since she is tired and busy with the baby and can see that Rashmi is being noticed.

grounding: Dadi hugs me first, not the baby, and says I am her special one; I feel safe and important again.

passage: The hospital corridor smelled of soap. Tenzin held his papa Deepak's hand tightly outside the ward. Everyone was going in to see the new baby. Then Dadi came out, walked straight past the flowers, and scooped Tenzin up first. "There's my special one!" she said, pressing her cheek to his. Tenzin hid his face in her shawl and smiled. Deepak laughed. "Dadi missed you most." Dadi carried Tenzin into the ward on her hip. "Now, show me your baby brother. You can tell me his name." Tenzin pointed proudly at the cot.

qa.q: Whom did Dadi scoop up first?
What does Tenzin hiding his face and smiling suggest?
qa.a: He felt safe, loved and important again after feeling left out while everyone went in to see the baby.

qa.q: How could other relatives follow Dadi's example?
qa.a: They could greet the older child first and give him a proud job, like telling everyone the baby's name.

qa.q: How might Deepak see Dadi's hug?
qa.a: He may feel grateful that his mother noticed Tenzin and helped him feel he still matters.

grounding: A grandmother greets the older child first at the hospital, helping him feel safe and important during the new-baby time.

passage:
Friday: Guests crowded around the new baby. Aditi sat on the stairs, chewing her plait. Papa, Ramesh, was busy pouring tea.
Saturday: Dadi arrived from the village with a bag of guavas. She put her bag down and hugged Aditi first, tight and long. "You are my special one." Aditi giggled into her sari.
Monday: Dadi and Aditi fed the ducks at the lake while the baby slept at home. "Dadi, the baby is still small," Aditi said. "I'll teach him ducks later." She skipped all the way back.

qa.q: What did Dadi bring from the village?
qa.a: Dadi brought a bag of guavas.

qa.q: How was Aditi feeling on Friday on the stairs?
qa.a: She felt left out and invisible while guests crowded around the new baby and Papa was busy.

qa.q: What did Dadi do that protected Aditi from feeling replaced?
qa.a: She hugged Aditi first, called her special and took her on a duck outing just for the two of them.

qa.q: How might Ramesh feel seeing Aditi skip back?
qa.a: He probably feels relieved and thankful that Dadi noticed what he was too busy to see.

grounding: Over a few days, a grandmother's first hug and special time help an older child feel safe and important after a new baby arrives.
